WEIGHTED GENERATING-CHART COMPACTNESS AND ITS EXACT DUAL LIMIT
ROOT mathematical derivation, 11 November 2026

1. The new obstruction is a chart obstruction, not a physical blow-up

P1_257E52_FULL_FINAL_20261111.md proves actual concentration removal for general
bounded-L4 compatible fields, and actual determinant-one approximation for
smooth maps with U_x>=0. It also exhibits bounded physical gradients with
unbounded unweighted Lp Hessians in the generating chart, for every p>1.
Thus a uniform unweighted Hessian bound is unavailable. The following lift uses
the actual source probability instead. It is not an assumption that a weak
limit is a single gradient, a quasiconvexity theorem or an exact moment oracle.

Let W(theta,y) be smooth and periodic, M=D^2W=[[a,c],[c,b]], q=1+c>0, and
  F=D Psi=q^{-1}[[1,-b],[a,q^2-ab]], det F=1.
The source coordinate change has actual Jacobian q. All measures below live
on the chart torus with its fixed Haar measure lambda=dtheta dy. Put
  mu=q lambda,  mathsf M=M lambda,  tau=(det M)lambda,
  r=1/q, Z=M/q, h=(det M)/q.
The exact finite-field relations are
  d lambda=r d mu, d mathsf M=Z d mu, d tau=h d mu,
  Z12=1-r, det Z=r h,
  F=Fcal(r,Z,h)=[[r,-Z22],[Z11,2-h-r]].                  (1)
In particular F is AFFINE in the lifted densities, although their algebraic
constraint is nonlinear. These identities preserve the actual source measure.

2. A uniformly bounded compact family of measures

Periodicity gives
  mu(T2)=1,
  both coordinate marginals of mu are unit Haar,
  mathsf M=D^2W as a distribution, int mathsf M=0,
  int tau=0, mu=lambda+mathsf M12.                       (2)
The two marginal identities follow by integrating W12 in either coordinate.
The last null-minor identity uses int W11 W22=int W12^2.

If E=int_original |F|^4, then det F=1 implies |F|^2>=2. From (1),
  r^4<=|F|^4,
  |Z|^2<=4+4|F|^2<=6|F|^2,
  |h|^4=|2-tr F|^4<=64|F|^4.
Consequently
  int(r^4+|Z|^4+|h|^4)d mu<=128E.                      (3)
In particular mathsf M and tau have bounded total variation, and mu is a
probability measure with both marginals fixed. No unweighted Lp bound on M or
q, p>1, has been asserted.
